title: 1956 Montgolfier vacuum tests in Paris

tellings.quote: But in 1956, Jean-Louis Cornillon, a French Air Force officer and technical representative for one of France's largest aircraft companies, Sud Aviation, facilitated Brown's experiments in a vacuum in the Montgolfier facility in Paris.

plain: In 1956, the inventor Townsend Brown is said to have tested his devices in a vacuum at the Montgolfier facility in Paris. Michels tells it, drawing on a writer named Paul Schatzkin and a document he calls the Montgolfier report: a French Air Force officer named Jean-Louis Cornillon, "technical representative for one of France's largest aircraft companies, Sud Aviation," arranged the experiments. If true, it would mean a major French aircraft maker took Brown's work seriously enough to test it.
